short_description: Consumer-facing physical trait that reports a cautious panel-relative signal related to appendicular lean mass tendency within the current local reference panel.
summary_note: Usable consumer-facing physical trait with workable raw-array support and a narrower interpretation boundary focused on appendicular lean mass, meaning lean tissue in the limbs, rather than whole-body composition for the no-imputation workflow.
what_it_measures: A panel-relative polygenic signal associated with appendicular lean mass tendency, meaning lean mass in the arms and legs, calibrated within the current local empirical reference panel.
interpretation_template: Appendicular lean mass tendency is presented here as a cautious panel-relative body-composition signal, not as a direct measurement of current muscle size, athletic performance, or gym response. {interpretation}
caution_text: Use as a cautious panel-relative signal only. No imputation or ancestry-adjusted normalization is used, and the output should not be treated as a deterministic real-world result, a direct body-composition measurement, or fitness advice.
limitations: Percentiles and z-scores are relative to the local reference panel, not to a population-wide benchmark.

Real-world appendicular lean mass depends strongly on sex, age, hormones, training, nutrition, illness, medication use, and hydration status, so this should not be treated as a precise estimate of current limb muscle mass.
The source phenotype targets appendicular lean mass rather than total body composition, so interpretation should stay narrower than a general statement about whole-body build.
confidence_note: Confidence reflects overlap and reference robustness under the no-imputation raw-array workflow, not certainty about the real-world trait.
reference_note: Percentiles and z-scores are calibrated against a local empirical reference artifact built from raw-array files in this project; they are panel-relative, not population-wide.
